corrected_answer: Scope and assumptions for NCCL variant 8: treat the larger-world-size hang as an unproven synchronization or communication failure. First reproduce with a minimal collective and a binary-search sequence of world sizes, then compare the known-good reduced world, alternate rank mappings, explicit interface/NIC affinity, and a control-plane-only rendezvous. Correlate all records by job, rank, attempt, and timestamp, redact identifiers, and preserve raw evidence. Use least-privilege read-only checks first; do not broadly open firewall ports, change MTU, or restart production services. Change one authorized variable at a time in an isolated canary, with a no-change control and repeated matched trials. Predeclare success as communicator formation and the collective completing across the target world size with zero hangs/timeouts, correct outputs, and no new link errors, reporting success rate, time-to-form, collective latency (ms), timeout/error rate, bandwidth (GB/s), and retry/retransmit counts with denominators and uncertainty. source_user: Advanced cluster case multi-node NCCL-17: A multi-node NCCL job hangs only at larger world sizes. Produce a falsifiable diagnosis and rollback plan. Variant 17 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: test rank mapping, interface selection, topology, NIC affinity, rendezvous, firewall and ports, timeout logs, communicator formation, reduced-world baselines, and network counters. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: Scope and assumptions for NCCL variant 17: treat the larger-world-size hang as an unproven synchronization or communication failure. Pin and record NCCL, CUDA, driver, framework, launcher, container, fabric (InfiniBand/RoCE), node/GPU/rank mapping, NIC and NUMA affinity, selected interface, routing/MTU, rendezvous endpoint, ports/firewall policy, topology, collective/message shape, timeout settings, and whether the observation is measured or estimated. Do not claim a platform-specific cause without artifacts. Falsifiable hypothesis: variant 17 fails when a particular rank pair, topology edge, interface choice, rendezvous participant, or communicator-formation path introduced at the larger world size is exercised; the failure should disappear or move under a controlled change to that factor while software, message shape, load, and timeout remain fixed. First reproduce with a minimal collective and a binary-search sequence of world sizes, then compare the known-good reduced world, alternate rank mappings, explicit interface/NIC affinity, and a control-plane-only rendezvous. Capture per-rank membership and ordering, communicator state, NCCL debug timestamps and transport selection, launcher/rendezvous logs, timeout location, endpoint reachability, connection/packet counters, link/port errors, retransmits, GPU/NIC telemetry, and synchronized start/end times with units. Correlate all records by job, rank, attempt, and timestamp, redact identifiers, and preserve raw evidence. Use least-privilege read-only checks first; do not broadly open firewall ports, change MTU, or restart production services. Change one authorized variable at a time in an isolated canary, with a no-change control and repeated matched trials. Predeclare success as communicator formation and the collective completing across the target world size with zero hangs/timeouts, correct outputs, and no new link errors, reporting success rate, time-to-form, collective latency (ms), timeout/error rate, bandwidth (GB/s), and retry/retransmit counts with denominators and uncertainty. If a canary hangs, corrupts output, exceeds the timeout/error or link-error budget, or cannot be rolled back cleanly, stop, terminate the job safely, restore the prior rank/interface/topology configuration, verify process and communicator cleanup, and return to the reduced-world or known-good mapping. Escalate to fabric/launcher owners when evidence is insufficient; do not present correlation as root-cause proof.
